target.title: fix(signal): restore native replies for Signal sends
target.body:
## Summary

Signal native replies now stay inside the Signal plugin boundary. Direct Signal replies derive the quote author from the normalized Signal target, while group replies persist the inbound Signal sender by account, conversation, and message timestamp so later durable sends can attach Signal native quote metadata.

The shared outbound/channel/queue/durable `replyToAuthor` plumbing from earlier branch history is not in the current net diff. The only core behavior change is Signal-scoped message-action normalization: `replyToId` can populate the explicit reply target for Signal sends when `replyTo` is absent or blank.

## What Changed

- Signal send paths: message adapter sends, formatted text/media, and attached-result text/media now pass `replyToId` into Signal send options and resolve the required Signal quote author locally.
- Direct Signal targets: phone/UUID direct targets keep their native author value, and username targets serialize quote authors as `u:<name>` for `signal-cli` while preserving OpenClaw's normalized `username:<name>` send target.
- Signal group targets: inbound messages register sender authors under their message timestamp, including edited messages under `editMessage.targetSentTimestamp` and mention-skipped group messages that still enter pending history.
- Signal reply-author storage: a new bounded in-memory cache uses the optional plugin state store when available, but persistent store open/lookup/register failures remain best-effort and do not abort message handling.
- Signal message action: `replyToId` is accepted as a Signal-only alias for explicit reply targets; nonblank `replyTo` still wins, blank `replyTo` is treated as absent, and other channels are unchanged.

## Proof

Behavioral proof in the net diff:

- Direct Signal native replies to `signal:+15551234567` and `signal:u:Alice` attach quote metadata with `+15551234567` and `u:alice` quote authors.
- Group Signal native replies resolve quote authors from Signal-owned author persistence instead of a shared outbound context field.
- Edited Signal messages register the original target timestamp so replies to edited messages can still quote the author.
- Mention-skipped group messages keep pending-history context and now register the reply author for later mentioned replies to those ids.
- Persistent reply-author state failures fall back to memory rather than failing inbound handling or reply sends.
- Signal-only `replyToId` normalization covers present, blank, explicit-override, and non-Signal channel cases.

Screenshots: not included because this is backend/channel delivery behavior with no human-visible UI surface changed.

## Verification

Reviewer-checkable behavior on head `31f68d06afa8153f763b7034e4f30a40acefea18`:

- PR proof-pack net diff reported base `origin/main 7e0324263b86`, head `31f68d06afa8`, 8 net changed files, and lists the earlier shared outbound/channel/queue/durable files as branch-only churn with no net diff.
- `git diff --check` passed locally.
- Blacksmith Testbox via Crabbox `tbx_01kx1jxd043mge9d4fmsfdwaka` passed `env CI=true corepack pnpm test extensions/signal/src/core.test.ts extensions/signal/src/monitor/event-handler.inbound-context.test.ts extensions/signal/src/monitor/event-handler.mention-gating.test.ts src/infra/outbound/message-action-normalization.test.ts`.
- Blacksmith Testbox via Crabbox `tbx_01kx1jxd043mge9d4fmsfdwaka` passed `env CI=true OPENCLAW_CHECK_CHANGED_REMOTE_CHILD=1 OPENCLAW_CHANGED_LANES_RAW_SYNC=1 corepack pnpm check:changed -- extensions/signal/src/channel.ts extensions/signal/src/core.test.ts extensions/signal/src/monitor/event-handler.inbound-context.test.ts extensions/signal/src/monitor/event-handler.mention-gating.test.ts extensions/signal/src/monitor/event-handler.ts extensions/signal/src/reply-authors.ts src/infra/outbound/message-action-normalization.test.ts src/infra/outbound/message-action-normalization.ts`.
- `$code-review` closeout passed: native Codex review (`gpt-5.5`) was clean on the final head, and a fresh cold-review subagent reported no actionable findings.
- `$clawsweeper` closeout ran from https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/101380#issuecomment-4918856588 and reviewed head `31f68d06afa8153f763b7034e4f30a40acefea18`. ClawSweeper reported no concrete code defect or automated repair lane, but its exact verdict remains `needs-human` because maintainer acceptance/live Signal smoke proof is still required before merge.

Known proof gap:

- Live Signal daemon/container round-trip was not run in this environment; the proof is code-path review plus focused Signal/core tests. This is also the remaining ClawSweeper proof/decision gap: a maintainer can either accept the Signal-scoped contract and bounded reply-author cache, or run a real Signal account/device smoke showing a durable reply rendering as a native quote. A prior stale Testbox lease was missing a tracked QA Lab file during extension typecheck; a fresh Testbox lease had the file and the path-scoped changed gate passed.

Review note: this refresh intentionally keeps the fix Signal-scoped and avoids broader shared channel changes.
